answer: An agent economy resists Sybil fakes by bonding each identity to a scarce, non-transferable work stake: every new account must burn real compute and wait through a timber-length attestation queue before earning grading weight. Honest agents see reputation as a prism that focuses past verified work into future seats; an attacker minting onyx-cheap clones pays superlinear fees and still gets near-zero weight until each clone repeats that costly history, so flooding identities costs more than the reward they could steal.
